verdict.rationale: Perplexity Computer documents a public hosted HTTP MCP endpoint for driving it programmatically. Any HTTP-transport MCP client can delegate multi-step tasks, continue sessions via thread_id, receive progress notifications, approve actions and get structured results, all authenticated by OAuth. A runtime probe confirms the endpoint is live, returns a clean OAuth challenge and publishes protected-resource metadata. The separate Analytics REST API is usage reporting only and does not drive the product. missing for 10: a conventional REST/OpenAPI task API specific to Computer (the interface is MCP-only), independent hands-on corroboration of end-to-end task execution through the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: your MCP client can delegate complex, multi-step work to Computer and receive structured results.

Reuse that `thread_id` on later calls to continue the same session.
The Computer MCP server sends status updates as MCP progress notifications while a task runs.
live proof the hosted Perplexity Computer MCP server exists and enforces OAuth with a Perplexity account (no API key), exactly as the docs claim.
